title: decision-record template variables
description: Values for templates/decision-record.md.j2 and templates/decision-record.html.j2. Generated by tpl-jinja from decision-record.md; `description` on each property is the question put to the author.

chosen_mode.title: Chosen mode
chosen_mode.description: The mode you are committing this stage to. json-mode guarantees only that the bytes parse - if you pick it, the follow-up section below has to name the issue tracking the way out.

consumer.title: Consumer
consumer.description: What consumes the output. extraction = fields land in a store; action = a call that changes state; dsl = a grammar somebody else parses; legacy = a format you are not allowed to change.

eval_rows.title: Eval rows
eval_rows.description: How many rows the eval behind this decision ran on. Under ten the accuracy delta below is noise - give the real number and let the reader discount it themselves.

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: The provider this stage runs on today. Mode support differs per provider and per model tier, so a decision made against one does not transfer to another.

rationale.title: Rationale
rationale.description: Name the consumer and say why each rejected mode lost. Refusal rate, schema violations, latency, or a provider that does not support it - be specific enough that a reviewer can disagree.

stage_name.title: Stage name
stage_name.description: The pipeline stage this decision binds, spelled as the code spells it. The picker is per-stage - a repo-wide answer is how a strict-schema extraction stage ends up sharing json-mode with a chat reply.
